texts.li: [once,lowtech] The rider from {FACTION} is back, smiling this time. Last time's goods were counted at home and came out right, with nothing spoiled, so they want the same again: {TALE}, for {COUNT} silver. The rider has brought a small gift for the colony's trouble.\n\nAs before, they'll send for it in five days, and it's the whole order or none of it.

[once,!lowtech] {FACTION}'s new order came in today, written on the back of the old one.\n\n"Received in good condition, count correct. Same again: {TALE}, {COUNT} silver on collection. Collecting in five days. Full order or nothing. Something for your trouble comes with this note."

[again] By now {FACTION}'s quartermaster doesn't bother to haggle. The order came with a small gift, as it always does, and reads much like the last one: {TALE}, {COUNT} silver, collected in five days.

[again,winter] Winter has made {FACTION} steady customers. Their rider stamped the snow off at the gate, handed over a small gift, and asked for {TALE} again, at {COUNT} silver.\n\nThey'll send for it in five days, the whole order or none of it.

li.label: Take the order
li.outcome: The colony sends back its word. {FACTION} will come for {TALE} in five days.

li.label: Not this time
li.outcome: Word goes back that the colony is turning the order down. {FACTION} will buy elsewhere from now on, and won't ask again.

remembered.li: [once] {FACTION} bought {THING} from the colony once, and were pleased with it.
[again] {FACTION} come to the colony for {THING} now, and no longer haggle.

texts.li: {A_nameDef}'s {RELATION}, {X_nameDef}, is waiting at the gate with no weapon and the dust of {FACTION}'s roads on {X_possessive} boots. Somebody back home talked, and the family has known for a while where {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} went when they ran.\n\n{X_nameDef} came alone, and says talking is all {X_pronoun} wants.

[mother] A woman of {FACTION} has been asking for {A_nameDef} at the gate since dawn. It's {X_nameDef}, {A_possessive} mother. She has brought a basket of things from home, and hasn't decided yet whether she's angry.\n\n{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} have seen her from the window and haven't gone out yet.

[father,lowtech] {X_nameDef}, {A_nameDef}'s father, rode in from {FACTION}'s lands this morning on a borrowed mule. He has asked for {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} by name, and says he only wants to talk.\n\nThe last time the family talked, the two of them left in the night.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} came up the road this morning asking for {A_nameDef}. {X_nameDef} is {A_possessive} {RELATION}, and it took most of a season to work out where {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} had gone.\n\n{X_nameDef} says the family only wants to talk. {A_nameDef} isn't sure that's all.

li.label: Let them talk
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} talked with {X_nameDef} behind a shut door for most of the day, and the voices never rose. {X_nameDef} set off for home afterwards with a letter for the family, and said {X_pronoun} would come again.
li.riskOutcome: The talk starts well and goes wrong in the second hour, over the family's good name. {X_nameDef} is gone before supper, and {A_nameDef} has shut {A_possessive} door.

li.label: Send a gift home ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} counted the silver, put it away without comment, and set off home with a message for the family. It isn't forgiveness. Still, {FACTION} have spoken more kindly of the colony since.

li.label: Ask {X_objective} to leave
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} was walked back to the road and asked not to come again, and looked back once at the windows before going. {FACTION} will hear of it.

remembered.li: The families of {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} among {FACTION} know where the two of them went.

texts.li: [lowtech] A peddler on the road from {FACTION}'s lands left a parcel tied with twine, and a letter for {A_nameDef} from {X_nameDef}, {A_possessive} {RELATION}, who visited a while back.\n\n"The goats are well. The miller's roof came down in the rain at last, as we always said it would, and he is living with his sister until it is mended. Your cousin has married the cooper's boy. Write and tell us if you are eating."

[!lowtech] A letter for {A_nameDef} came in with a passing trader today, along with a small parcel. {X_nameDef}, {A_possessive} {RELATION}, writes from {FACTION}'s lands that the crops came in late, the neighbor's boy has finally left home, and the old generator still needs kicking twice to start.

[winter] The parcel came wrapped against the snow, and the letter with it is a winter letter: short days, a cough going round, the well frozen solid twice already. It's from {X_nameDef}, {A_nameDef}'s {RELATION}, by way of a passing trader.\n\n{X_nameDef} ends by asking after each of the people {A_nameDef} wrote about last time, by name.

[summer] A dried flower fell out of the letter when {A_nameDef} opened it, and a parcel came along too. {X_nameDef}, {A_possessive} {RELATION}, writes that the summer has been long and dry among {FACTION}, and that the bees, at least, have never done better.

[spring] {X_nameDef}, {A_nameDef}'s {RELATION}, has written from {FACTION}'s lands. There's been a wedding, the spring floods took out the lower bridge, and a parcel came along with the letter. {A_nameDef} has been reading the good parts aloud to anyone who stops.

[fall] A trader passing through left a letter and a parcel for {A_nameDef}. It's from {X_nameDef}, {A_possessive} {RELATION}: the harvest was fair, the roof held, and the family still sets a place for {A_objective} at the long table on feast days.

The letter for {A_nameDef} is a page of small news from home. Somebody's had a baby, somebody else got married, and a dog went missing for a week and came back fat. {X_nameDef}, {A_possessive} {RELATION}, who visited a while ago, sent it with a parcel.

[past:farmer] A trader brought {A_nameDef} a letter and a parcel from {X_nameDef}, {A_possessive} {RELATION}. Most of it is about the fields back home: which strip flooded, which one finally took the barley, and who borrowed the plow and never brought it back.\n\nThe parcel smells of home. {A_nameDef} hasn't opened it yet, only held it.

[trait:Nervous] {A_nameDef} turned the letter over three times before opening it, sure it held bad news. It didn't. {X_nameDef}, {A_possessive} {RELATION}, only writes to say that they're all well, the roof is mended and the plum tree fruited at last, and sends a parcel along with it.\n\n{A_nameDef} has been smiling at nothing all afternoon.

[skill:Artistic] {X_nameDef}, {A_nameDef}'s {RELATION}, has written from {FACTION}'s lands, and drawn the old house in the margin so {A_nameDef} would know what it looks like now. The drawing is terrible. {A_nameDef} has pinned it over {A_possessive} bed anyway.\n\nA parcel came with the letter, wrapped in a scarf {A_nameDef} remembers.

[trait:Kind] A letter came for {A_nameDef} today from {X_nameDef}, {A_possessive} {RELATION}, with a parcel tied up in string. Half of the letter is questions: is {A_nameDef} eating, is {A_pronoun} warm enough, are the people here good to {A_objective}.\n\n{A_nameDef} has started a reply that is already longer than the letter.

[past:soldier] {A_nameDef} has a letter from {X_nameDef}, {A_possessive} {RELATION}, and a parcel with it. {X_nameDef} never asks about the old days in the army, and doesn't now. The letter is all small things: a new well, a neighbor's wedding, the price of salt.\n\n{A_nameDef} read it standing up, then sat down and read it again.

li.label: Write back
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} spends the evening on the reply, crossing out more than {A_pronoun} keeps. The next trader heading that way will carry it.

outcomes.li: [trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} writes four pages back and asks after every person in the letter by name, and a few who weren't in it.
[past:soldier] {A_nameDef} writes back in the short square hand of someone used to writing reports, then adds a postscript about the colony that runs on for two pages.
[trait:Abrasive] {A_nameDef} writes back. It's short, and it complains about the weather twice, but it ends with "love" and that is more than {A_nameDef} usually says.

li.label: Invite {X_objective} to come and live here
li.outcome: {A_nameDef}'s reply asks {X_nameDef} to come and live at the colony. If {X_nameDef} can get away from home, the journey takes a few days.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} writes back the same evening that there's a bed here, and work, and a place at the table. If {X_nameDef} can get away, it's a few days on the road.
[trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} writes that {X_nameDef} should come, and needn't bring anything but warm clothes. If {X_nameDef} can get away, the journey takes a few days.

li.label: Send a parcel home (30 silver)
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sews the coin into the toe of a sock, wraps it in a letter full of the colony's news, and gives the parcel to the next trader heading that way. {FACTION} think the better of the colony for it.

outcomes.li: [skill:Crafting] {A_nameDef} packs a parcel for home with coin sewn into the lining and a carved box {A_pronoun} made in the evenings, and writes a letter to go with it.
[trait:Greedy] {A_nameDef} packs a parcel for home, and only counts the coin twice before tying it up.

li.label: Read it out at supper
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} read the letter out after supper, every bit of small news from home, and by the end the table was asking after people it had never met.

outcomes.li: [trait:Abrasive] {A_nameDef} read the letter out at supper with remarks of {A_possessive} own on every relative in it. The table hadn't laughed that hard in weeks.
[skill:Social] {A_nameDef} read the letter out at supper and did all the voices. {X_nameDef}'s came out slow and fond, and got the biggest laugh.

coming.li: {X_nameDef}, {A_nameDef}'s {RELATION}, has been asked to come and live here. Expected within {DAYS}.
[winter] {X_nameDef}, {A_nameDef}'s {RELATION}, is on the winter roads to come and live here. Expected within {DAYS}, snow allowing.
{A_nameDef} has asked {X_nameDef} to come and live here, and keeps looking down the road. Expected within {DAYS}.

done.li: [lowtech] {X_nameDef}, {A_nameDef}'s {RELATION}, walked in from {FACTION}'s lands today with a pack and a walking stick, and everything else left behind. {A_nameDef} knew that walk from a long way off and ran down the road to meet {X_objective}.\n\n{X_nameDef} has joined the colony.
[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} came up the road with two bags and a coat too warm for the weather, and asked for {A_nameDef}. {A_nameDef}'s {RELATION} is here to stay.\n\n{X_nameDef} is a colonist now.

[winter] {X_nameDef} came in through the snow wrapped to the eyes in scarves, with a sack of things from home over one shoulder. {A_nameDef} took one look and ran for the gate.\n\n{A_nameDef}'s {RELATION} has come to stay, and is one of the colony now.

{X_nameDef} turned up at the gate with a bundle on {X_possessive} back and the letter {A_nameDef} sent, worn soft from reading. {A_nameDef} hasn't let go of {X_possessive} arm since.\n\n{X_nameDef} lives here now.

fail.li: {X_nameDef} wrote back. There's nothing {X_nameDef} would like better than to come, but someone at home is sick and there's nobody else to look after them. {A_nameDef} has put the letter away with the others.

A reply came from {X_nameDef}, {A_nameDef}'s {RELATION}. The harvest is late and the family needs every pair of hands, so the journey will have to wait. {X_nameDef} promises to come when the fields are in.
{X_nameDef} won't be coming after all. A grandchild is on the way among {FACTION}, and {X_nameDef} means to be there for it. The letter asks {A_nameDef} to visit instead.
[winter] {X_nameDef} wrote back that the passes are snowed shut until spring. {X_nameDef} means to come when the roads open, and has sent a pair of mittens on ahead. {A_nameDef} wears them every day.

{X_nameDef}'s family has talked {X_objective} out of it. The roads are bad, they say, and the news on them is worse. {X_nameDef} still writes that {X_pronoun} will come one day, and {A_nameDef} believes it.

cancelled.li: Word came from {FACTION}'s lands that {X_nameDef} won't be coming to the colony after all.
{X_nameDef}'s journey to the colony is off. A trader from {FACTION}'s lands brought the news, and no more of it than that.
{X_nameDef} won't be coming. The news came secondhand, by way of a trader, who couldn't say why.

remembered.li: {X_nameDef}, {A_nameDef}'s {RELATION}, writes now and then from {FACTION}'s lands.
{A_nameDef} keeps the letters from {X_nameDef}, {A_possessive} {RELATION}, tied in a bundle by the bed.

texts.li: [winter] {A_nameDef} slipped on the ice outside the storeroom and went most of the way down the path on {A_possessive} back, holding a full jug up in the air the whole way. Not a drop spilled.\n\n"That was it," {A_nameDef} said from the bottom of the path. "That was the fortune teller's bad luck."

[lowtech] A roof tile came off in the wind and burst on the ground where {A_nameDef} had been standing a breath before.\n\n{A_nameDef} looked at the pieces for a long moment, then went to tell the others that the fortune teller's bad card had been played, and that was the end of it.

[!lowtech] Since the cards were read, {A_nameDef} has kept glancing up at the sky. Today a loose sheet of roofing came down in the wind, a step behind {A_objective}, and the glancing has stopped. Whatever the fortune teller saw coming, {A_nameDef} says, has come and gone.

[summer] Cutting brush by the fields, {A_nameDef} knocked down a wild bees' nest and ran with half the swarm behind. Not one of them stung.\n\n{A_nameDef} counts that as the bad luck in the fortune teller's cards, used up, and has been in a fine mood all day.

[spring|fall] Some animal came out of the undergrowth at a dead run, so close it brushed {A_nameDef}'s sleeve, and was gone before {A_nameDef} could shout.\n\nThe fortune teller's bad luck, {A_nameDef} has decided. Good riddance to it.

[child] {A_nameDef} climbed onto the storeroom roof after a lost ball and couldn't get down again. Two of the grown-ups fetched a ladder, and {A_nameDef} came down without a scratch.\n\nThe fortune teller's bad card has been on {A_nameDef}'s mind for days. Now {A_nameDef} is telling anyone who'll listen that the bad luck is used up.

Ever since the fortune teller turned up a bad card for {A_nameDef}, {A_nameDef} has been waiting for it to come true. Today, on the way down to the stores with a full basket, {A_nameDef} missed a step and landed sitting on the bottom one with the basket upright in {A_possessive} lap, without a bruise.\n\nThat, {A_nameDef} has decided, was it.

[skill:Animals] One of the colony's animals spooked at nothing, bolted straight at {A_nameDef}, swerved at the last moment and went on into the fields.\n\n{A_nameDef} watched it go, said "There. That was the cards," and went back to work whistling.

[skill:Cooking] A full kettle slid off its hook while {A_nameDef} was cooking and landed a hand's width from {A_possessive} feet, without a drop on {A_objective}.\n\n{A_nameDef} hung it back up and told the kitchen at large that the fortune teller could keep the rest of the cards. The bad luck had its chance, and missed.

[trait:Nervous] A shutter banged in the wind right behind {A_nameDef}, who jumped so hard {A_pronoun} dropped an armful of firewood on {A_possessive} own boots. Nothing worse came of it.\n\nSince the fortune teller's visit {A_nameDef} has jumped at every noise. This one, {A_nameDef} has decided, was the bad fortune itself, and the jumping has mostly stopped.

[spring] A rotten fence rail gave way as {A_nameDef} leaned on it, and {A_nameDef} sat down hard in the mud, unhurt and laughing. A muddy coat, {A_nameDef} says, is a cheap price for the fortune teller's bad luck.

[skill:Mining] A slab of loose rock came down in the cut where {A_nameDef} had been working a moment before, and broke into pieces on the floor.\n\n{A_nameDef} looked at the rubble for a long while. Then {A_nameDef} said the fortune teller's cards were paid in full, and went back in with a lighter step.

[trait:Optimist] A gust took {A_nameDef}'s hat clean off and sent it bowling away across the fields, and it hasn't been seen since.\n\nA lost hat. That's all the fortune teller's bad luck came to, {A_nameDef} says, and the stars have done their worst.

[sided,lowtech] A rider of {FACTION} came by today leading a pack horse, and unloaded {TALE} with their people's thanks. When {FACTION} quarreled with {ENEMY}, the colony took their side. They haven't forgotten.\n\nBy all accounts, neither have {ENEMY}.

[sided,!lowtech] A drop pod came down from {FACTION} with {TALE} inside and a note in a heavy hand.

"We remember who stood with us against {ENEMY}."

Traders say {ENEMY} still bring it up whenever the colony is mentioned.

[middle,mediator] The middle way {A_nameDef} found between {FACTION} and {ENEMY} has held all season. Both peoples sent word, and something with it: {TALE}.\n\n{A_nameDef} has pinned the two messages up side by side.
[middle,!mediator,lowtech] Neither {FACTION} nor {ENEMY} has broken the peace the colony worked out between them, and both have sent word to say so. With the word came {TALE}, sent by both.

[middle,!mediator,!lowtech] {FACTION} and {ENEMY} have both sent word, which hasn't happened since their quarrel. The colony's settlement is holding, and a drop pod has come down with {TALE} from the two of them.

remembered.li: [sided] {FACTION} remember that the colony took their side against {ENEMY}.
[middle] {FACTION} and {ENEMY} remember the middle way the colony found in their quarrel.

texts.li: [heal,lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has walked two days nursing an arm that was set crooked last winter and never healed straight. People on the road said to ask for {TALE}, and {TALE} turns out to be {A_nameDef}.

[heal,!lowtech] "Is this where {TALE} lives?" {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} asked at the gate, between coughs. The cough has lasted all season, and the doctor at home has run out of ideas. The one {X_nameDef} wants is {A_nameDef}.

[build] {FACTION} are raising a new hall, and the walls keep cracking. {X_nameDef}, who has the building of it, has come with a roll of drawings under one arm to ask for a day of {A_nameDef}'s advice. Talk of {TALE} has carried that far.

[dig] A mine that keeps flooding, and a crew that has started talking about giving up. {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to ask {A_nameDef}, known on the roads as {TALE}, where the water is getting in.

[grow] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come with a sack of seed and a question. Their fields have done badly three years running, and {X_nameDef} has heard that the colony's {A_nameDef}, called {TALE}, could grow barley on a rock.

[cook] Travelers who have eaten at the colony won't stop talking about the cooking of the one they call {TALE}. {X_nameDef}, who cooks for a big household among {FACTION}, has come to see whether it's true, and to beg {A_nameDef} for a recipe.

[beasts] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} came in holding an empty halter. The young draft animal it belongs to won't take a harness, and {X_nameDef} has heard that the colony's {A_nameDef}, called {TALE}, can calm anything with four legs.
[hunt] The hunters of {FACTION} have had a lean season. {X_nameDef} has come to ask {A_nameDef}, the one they call {TALE}, where the game goes when it leaves the valleys.
[study] {X_nameDef}, a student among {FACTION}, has a satchel of notes and three pages of questions, all of them for {A_nameDef}. Even {FACTION}'s students have heard of {TALE}.

[make] A chair leg snapped clean at the joint, and a bag of questions to go with it. {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has brought both for {A_nameDef}, known as {TALE}, because the carpenters at home can't say where the joint went wrong.
[talk] Two families of {FACTION} have been at odds over the same strip of grazing for a year. {X_nameDef}, from one of them, has come to ask {A_nameDef}, known as {TALE}, to help make their case.

[defend] {X_nameDef} speaks for a village of {FACTION} that has been raided twice this year. They all know of {TALE} in that village, {X_nameDef} says, and {X_nameDef} has come to ask {A_nameDef} how a small place holds out.

[bless] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is to be married at the next new moon, and the couple's own priest died in the winter. {X_nameDef} has come to the colony's {A_nameDef}, called {TALE}, for the words and a blessing to carry home.

[bless] A child was born in {X_nameDef}'s house among {FACTION}, small and early, and the family want the old words said over it properly. They sent {X_nameDef} the whole way on foot to ask {TALE}, which is to say {A_nameDef}.

[counsel] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has lost {X_possessive} faith, or thinks so, and can't talk about it at home. On the road {X_nameDef} heard of the colony's {A_nameDef}, the one they call {TALE}, and has come to sit with {A_objective} for a day.

[counsel] A quarrel among {FACTION} over what their faith allows has split {X_nameDef}'s family down the middle. {X_nameDef} has come to ask {A_nameDef}, known on the roads as {TALE}, what {A_pronoun} would tell them.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} help
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} gave {X_nameDef} the day. By evening {X_nameDef} had what {X_pronoun} came for, and left payment on the table before setting off home.

li.label: {A_nameDef} can't spare the day
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} nods, shoulders the pack again and starts back the way {X_pronoun} came.

texts.li: [killed,lowtech] The hunters came back early. A small band of {ENEMY} has made camp a few hours' walk away, resting on their way somewhere else. {A_nameDef} swore to make {ENEMY} pay for {DEAD}, and hasn't said a word since hearing it.\n\nThe colony could draw them out to fight here, on its own ground, or let them pass.

[killed,!lowtech] Scouts have spotted a small band of {ENEMY} camped in the hills, not far off. {A_nameDef} swore vengeance on {ENEMY} for {DEAD}, and is already checking {A_possessive} weapon.\n\nA few shots at their camp would bring them here, to fight on the colony's ground. Or the colony can leave them be.

[taken] {ENEMY} took {DEAD}. A small band of them is camped not far from the colony now, and {A_nameDef} has sworn they'll answer for it.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants them drawn out to fight here, on ground the colony knows. The council can agree, or let them move on.

[tribalfoe] Smoke is rising from a war camp of {ENEMY} in the hills, a few hours away. A small band, no more. {A_nameDef} swore vengeance on them for {DEAD}.\n\nIf the colony wants them, they can be drawn in to fight on its own ground. If not, they'll be gone in a day.

li.label: Draw them out
li.outcome: A few of the colony's people show themselves near the camp, then turn for home without hurrying. {ENEMY} take the bait. They'll be here within hours, and {A_nameDef} is ready.

li.label: {ENEMY} take the bait
li.text: The band of {ENEMY} followed the colony's people back, as planned, and they're here. {A_nameDef} swore they would answer for {DEAD}.

li.label: Let them pass
li.outcome: The band of {ENEMY} breaks camp the next morning and moves on. {A_nameDef} watches the smoke of their fires until it's gone.

texts.li: [first,guest] A year ago today, the first of the colony's people set down their packs here in the {PLACE} and argued about where to sleep. {A_nameDef} was one of them, and remembers that first night better than most of what came after.\n\n{X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, among the first neighbors to trade with the colony, has come to mark the day with a gift.

[first,noguest] "We had one pot," {A_nameDef} keeps telling people today, "and no two of us agreed what to cook in it." A year ago the colony was a handful of people and their packs in the {PLACE}, and {A_nameDef} has been here since the first night.

[years,guest] It's {COUNT} years today since the colony was founded. {A_nameDef} has been here the longest of anyone now, and can still point to the spot where the first fire was lit.\n\n{X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, an old friend of the colony, has come to mark the day and brought a gift.
[years,noguest] The colony is {COUNT} years old today. {A_nameDef} has been here longest of anyone, and remembers the {PLACE} when there was nothing in it but wind and one crooked shelter.
[years,lost,noguest] It's {COUNT} years today since the colony was founded. Not all who came are here to see it. {A_nameDef}, who has been here the longest, started the day at the graves.

[winter,first,noguest] A year ago today the colony was founded, in snow much like this. {A_nameDef} still remembers how cold that first night was in the {PLACE}, with no walls and not enough blankets.

li.label: Hold a feast
li.outcome: The founding feast ran until well past midnight. The old stories came out again, the first night and the first winter, and the first winter was colder every time it was told.

li.label: A quiet supper
li.outcome: Founding day went by with a quiet supper. At the end of it one cup was raised, and the words were kept short.

lines.li: To the ones who aren't here to see it.
To the first winter, and every one since.

li.label: Ask {A_nameDef} to tell the story of the first days
li.outcome: After supper {A_nameDef} stood up and told it from the start: the first night, the first winter, the first time the walls held. The newest colonists asked the most questions.

outcomes.li: [first] {A_nameDef} told the story of the colony's first year, start to finish. Said aloud, it sounded like a great deal more than one year.
[lost] {A_nameDef} told the story of the founding, and named each of those who came and aren't here anymore. A cup was raised to every name.

[years,lowtech] {A_nameDef} told the founding story by the hearth, the way it's told every year now, with the same pauses in the same places. The young ones knew most of it by heart and mouthed along.

li.label: the story of the first days

extra.li: [lost] Colonists who have died since the founding: {ITEM}.
[known] Travelers on the roads call the colony {ITEM}.
[lastfounder] Of those who were here on the first day, only {ITEM} is left, and lights the fire.
[founder] {ITEM}, the Founder, has seen ten years of it and more, and tells the story of the first night again.
[firstborn] The colony's first child, {ITEM}, is grown and sits with the adults tonight.

texts.li:
Over supper {A_nameDef} mentioned wanting to {GOAL}, and the traveler at the end of the table, {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, put down {X_possessive} spoon.

"I did that," {X_nameDef} said. "Took me years. Sit down and I'll tell you how."

The two of them talked until late, and {A_nameDef} came away with a head full of advice.

[skill] The traveler staying the night, {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, once set out to {GOAL} as well, and managed it. All evening {X_nameDef} has been going over {SKILL} with {A_nameDef}: what to practice, what to skip, and the mistakes that cost {X_objective} a year the first time round.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a traveler of {FACTION}, has stopped for the night. When {A_nameDef} talked about wanting to {GOAL}, {X_nameDef} laughed and said it had taken {X_objective} ten years to do the same. The two of them talked until the candles burned down.

[their:grateful] "Room on the wagons for friends," says the master of {FACTION}'s caravan, stopped in the road on the way to the market at {PLACE}. "Give us {TALE} and we'll bring you back {THING}. They pay better out there than anyone does here."\n\nThe colony is short of {THING}, and the caravan will be back this way in a week or so.

[lowtech] {FACTION}'s caravan has pulled up in the road with its oxen blowing, bound for the market at {PLACE}, a long way off. There's room on the wagons. Send {TALE} along, the caravan master says, and they'll trade it at {PLACE} for {THING}, which the colony is running low on.\n\nThey'll be back this way in a week or so.

[!lowtech] Room to spare, on the way to the market at {PLACE}: {FACTION}'s trader offers to carry {TALE} there, sell it, and come back with {THING} bought out of what it fetches. The colony is short of {THING}. The caravan expects to be back in a week or so.

[winter] The last caravan of the winter is going out from {FACTION} to the market at {PLACE}. Its master offers to take {TALE} from the colony's stores and trade it there for {THING}, which the colony has too little of.\n\nThey expect to be back in a week or so, snow permitting.

li.label: Send {TALE} with them
li.outcome: The caravan's people load {TALE} and set off for {PLACE}. They should be back in a week or so.

li.label: Not this time
li.outcome: The caravan moves on to {PLACE} without the colony's goods.

extra.li: Expected in return: about {COUNT} {THING}. In the colony's stores now: {ITEM}.

coming.li: {FACTION}'s caravan comes back from {PLACE} in about {DAYS}, with the colony's share: about {COUNT} {THING}.

done.li: [fair,lowtech] {FACTION}'s caravan came back from {PLACE} today, dusty and loud. What the colony sent sold well. They've unloaded its share at the trade spot: {ITEM}.
[fair,!lowtech] Good prices at {PLACE}. {FACTION}'s caravan is back, and the colony's share is waiting at the trade spot: {ITEM}.

[poor] {FACTION}'s caravan is back from {PLACE}, later than they'd hoped and short-tempered about it. Prices were poor this time. The colony's share, {ITEM}, is at the trade spot, and it's less than anyone expected.

cancelled.li: {FACTION}'s caravan never came back from {PLACE}, and neither did the colony's goods.

texts.li: [their:grateful] {FACTION}'s crier came to the colony before anywhere else, to say that the harvest fair at {PLACE} opens this week and that friends of {FACTION} are wanted there.\n\nA cart of {TALE} would sell well. {A_nameDef}, who grew most of it, thinks the best of it could take a prize.

[lowtech] "Harvest fair at {PLACE}, three days, judging on the last day." {FACTION}'s crier shouted it from the road without stopping, and went on to the next farm.\n\nThere'll be buyers from three valleys. The colony could send a cart of {TALE}, and {A_nameDef}, who grew most of it, has an eye on the judging.

[!lowtech] {FACTION} have invited the colony to their harvest fair at {PLACE}. There'll be buyers from all over, a few too many speeches, and a judging for the best produce.\n\nA cartload of {TALE} would sell well there, and {A_nameDef} wants to enter the best of it for the judging.

[harvesthome] Harvest home is close, and {FACTION} have sent word of their own harvest fair at {PLACE}. The colony could send a cart of {TALE}. {A_nameDef} has already been through the crop, setting the best of it aside for the judges.

li.label: Send a cart of {TALE}
li.outcome: The colony's {THING} goes off to {PLACE} on {FACTION}'s carts. The fair runs a few days, and they'll bring back what it fetches.

li.label: Not this year
li.outcome: The colony keeps its harvest at home this year.

extra.li: In the colony's stores now: {ITEM}. The cart should fetch about {COUNT} silver at the fair.

coming.li: The harvest fair at {PLACE} ends in about {DAYS}. {FACTION} will bring back what the colony's {THING} fetched.

done.li: [prize] The cart came back from {PLACE} empty, with {COUNT} silver and a ribbon. {A_nameDef}'s {THING} took the prize for the best of the harvest, and {A_nameDef} has pinned the ribbon up over the door.

[prize] First prize at {PLACE}. {FACTION} brought back the colony's share, {COUNT} silver, and the news that {A_nameDef}'s {THING} won the judging outright. {A_nameDef} has asked to hear every word the judges said.
[noprize] The cart came back from the fair at {PLACE} empty, with {COUNT} silver for the colony's {THING}. A farmer from the hills took the prize this year, for the third year running.
[noprize] The colony's {THING} sold before noon on the first day of the fair at {PLACE}, and {FACTION} have brought back {COUNT} silver for it. The judges gave their prize to someone else.

cancelled.li: The cart sent to the harvest fair at {PLACE} never came back.

IncidentDef.label: a guest on a winter night

texts.li: [lowtech] At dusk a lone traveler came in out of the {PLACE}, white with frost, and knocked at the gate. {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is on the way home and won't make it before dark. It's {TALE} outside and getting colder.\n\n{X_nameDef} asks for a place near the fire for the night, nothing more.

[!lowtech] A traveler came up the road at dusk, alone, with frost on {X_possessive} collar and a pack frozen stiff. {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} won't reach home tonight, and it's already {TALE}.\n\n{X_nameDef} asks to sleep somewhere warm and be gone in the morning.

[supper] It's the season of the midwinter supper, and at dusk a stranger knocked at the gate: {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, alone on the road and chilled through. It's {TALE} outside.\n\nThere's room at the table, if the colony wants to set another place.

[bitter] Three knocks at the gate, slow ones. It's {TALE} tonight, cold enough to kill, and {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} lost the road in the snow and followed the colony's lights in.\n\n{X_nameDef} asks only to get warm and stay until morning.

[meal] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} came to the gate as the light went, half frozen, on the way home from somewhere further than {X_pronoun} meant to go. It's {TALE} outside.\n\nThere's {THING} in the stores, enough to share, and {X_nameDef} asks only for a corner to sleep in.

li.label: Bring {X_objective} in
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} got a seat near the fire, a bowl of whatever was hot and a blanket for the night, and {A_nameDef} sat up talking with {X_objective} until late.

li.label: Send {X_objective} on with food
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is given bread, something hot to drink and directions to the nearest shelter, and goes back out into the dark.

li.label: Keep the gate shut
li.outcome: The gate stays shut. After a while {X_nameDef} gives up knocking and goes back out into the cold.

outcomes.li: [soldier] {A_nameDef} sat up late with the guest, trading soldiering stories, and told {X_nameDef} a few the colony had never heard.
[outlaw] Late in the night, with only the guest to hear it, {A_nameDef} talked about {A_possessive} outlaw years and told {X_nameDef} things {A_pronoun} had never told anyone here.
[noble] Wrapped in a blanket, {X_nameDef} listened until late while {A_nameDef} talked about the great house {A_pronoun} grew up in, and the winters there, with servants to keep every fire going.
[healer] {A_nameDef} warmed {X_nameDef}'s hands with a hot stone wrapped in cloth, an old healer's trick, and the two of them talked until late.
[scholar] {A_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} argued happily about the winter stars until the fire was down to embers.
[farmer] {A_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} talked seed and soil until late, the way farmers do in winter when there's nothing in the ground to tend.
[trader] By the end of the evening, {A_nameDef} had got every scrap of news about prices on the roads out of {X_nameDef}, and given away none of the colony's.
[artisan] {A_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} turned out to know some of the same old work songs, and sang a few before bed, low, so as not to wake the others.

done.li: {X_nameDef} was gone before anyone was up, and had left {TALE} behind by way of thanks.
Gone at first light, {X_nameDef} left the colony {TALE} for its trouble.
{X_nameDef} thanked whoever was awake, set down {TALE} for the colony, and went out into the morning cold.

texts.li: [first] The colony's first spring in the {PLACE}. The drifts have gone soft and gray, the ground under them is mud, and people keep finding reasons to work outside.\n\n{A_nameDef} turned up {TALE} in the melt, lost by some traveler over the winter.

[again] Meltwater is running off every roof, the paths are mud to the ankle, and there's green showing where the drifts were deepest. After the long winter, the colony is glad of it, mud and all.\n\nOut by the road the melt gave up {TALE}. {A_nameDef} was the one who spotted it.

[nameyear] The snow is going, and the talk at supper has already turned to what to call the new year, and whether the muffalo is still a serious suggestion.\n\n{A_nameDef} has found {TALE} half-buried in the last of the snow.
[child] {A_nameDef} came running in with muddy knees to say the snow by the gate had melted down to grass. The thaw has come.\n\n{A_nameDef} also found {TALE} in the mud, and is very proud of it.
